title: Publish the residual on a fixed weekly clock, starting now
problem: A residual that appears only when someone feels like computing it is not a track record.
what_changes: A dated origination board per week: our number, the market number (blank until licensed) and the residual, with the clock time of the capture.
risk: The market column stays blank until a licence exists, so the board looks incomplete.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: residuals measured against a closing snapshot beat the market in the majority of weeks with an interval excluding zero. Refutes: no systematic edge, or a residual series that only exists when the market column is blank.

title: Add a second season before promoting anything
problem: 89 out-of-sample games cannot separate skill from noise; the interval already crosses zero.
what_changes: Extend the corpus to the previous season with the identical frozen method, and re-run the same gate.
risk: Historic official pages may not expose the same fields.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: the lower bound clears zero on two seasons. Refutes: the second season reverses the sign, which would mean the first was noise.

title: Store the injury report on a fixed Wednesday-to-kickoff schedule
problem: One snapshot cannot be replayed, so no availability feature is possible.
what_changes: A dated capture per day with a hash, a timestamp and a schema check that fails on change.
risk: Storage grows; the page's layout may change without notice.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: designations visibly move during the week, which is the signal. Refutes: designations are final by Wednesday, in which case one weekly capture suffices.

title: Join designations to official inactive lists and publish the play rate
problem: Nobody knows what 'Questionable' means numerically, and old percentages were not derived from official lists.
what_changes: A table of designation to observed play rate with n and a confidence interval, per season.
risk: Inactive lists may not be published in a storable form.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: play rates differ sharply by designation. Refutes: all designations play at similar rates, in which case the label is not a usable feature.

title: Refuse the depth feature until an official ordering source exists
problem: Depth order is the input to every starter/backup claim, and the league route 404s.
what_changes: A published refusal with the 404 evidence, and a per-club feasibility table instead of an invented ordering.
risk: Removes a feature the brief explicitly asks for.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: fewer than 32 clubs publish a structured order, so the refusal stands. Refutes: an official route covering all 32 clubs is found, which would unblock the feature and reverse the decision.

title: Replace 'missing starter penalty' with an ablation harness
problem: A fixed points penalty for an absence is a guess dressed as a parameter.
what_changes: Run the identical model twice, with and without verified availability features, on a chronological holdout, and publish the difference with its interval.
risk: Requires the dated series first, so it cannot ship this week.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: the difference has an interval excluding zero. Refutes: availability adds nothing measurable, which is a legitimate and useful finding.

title: Rank on benchmark-relative Brier skill, and show the control row
problem: Win rate and short-run return cannot distinguish skill from variance.
what_changes: Every board carries its controls (coin flip, home base rate, favourites) beside the model, with intervals.
risk: The board will look empty, because almost nothing passes.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: a model beats the home base rate with an interval excluding zero. Refutes: nothing does, so the board correctly stays empty.

title: Put the luck share on the dashboard, not only in a paper
problem: A lucky staking run can mask a poor signal if only returns are shown.
what_changes: A panel publishing the share of club-win dispersion that a coin flip could have produced, recomputed each refresh.
risk: A single number invites over-reading.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports the panel: the luck share stays materially above zero. Refutes: luck share is near zero, which would make the panel unnecessary.

title: Keep every market column blank and visible until licensed
problem: A blank that is quietly filled with a scraped number is indistinguishable from a verified one.
what_changes: A published price policy: blank plus a flag plus the exact thing that would clear it.
risk: The site looks less complete.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: a licensed source arrives and the column fills with citation. Refutes: no licensable source exists, in which case the blank is permanent and should say so.

title: Make the standings reconciliation a CI gate everywhere
problem: A stale game log silently biases every rating.
what_changes: Run the 192-comparison standings check on every push and fail the build on one mismatch.
risk: A source outage fails the build for an unrelated reason.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: the gate catches a real transcription error, which it already did in this session. Refutes: the gate produces false failures from unstable pages, which would need a data not a code fix.

title: Publish a 'what would change our mind' field on every entry
problem: A one-sided claim cannot be audited.
what_changes: A mandatory second column naming the observation that would refute the entry.
risk: Adds prose that can go stale.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: reviewers cite the refutation column when rejecting a proposal. Refutes: the column stays empty in practice, meaning it is decoration.

title: Show the questions register, ranked by what they unblock
problem: A long question list is a reading exercise, not a decision aid.
what_changes: Sort each question by the number of downstream requirements it blocks, and show that count.
risk: Ranking can create false precision.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: the owner closes questions in rank order. Refutes: the owner closes none, meaning the block is authority rather than information.

title: Publish a per-team view: who is out, who the club lists next, and the count
problem: A team-level decision needs one screen, not thirty rows.
what_changes: One row per club: injured count from the official report, and an explicit blank where no official replacement order exists.
risk: The replacement column will be mostly blank without Q11.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: the club lists a next man for most positions. Refutes: the club publishes no ordering, in which case only the count column survives.

title: Add venue and roof to the fixture table as sourced facts
problem: Totals and passing props depend on wind and roof.
what_changes: A venue column cited to Game Center, and a blank roof column until an official designation exists.
risk: Roof designations change late and may not be archived.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: venue explains part of the total error. Refutes: no measurable effect, making the column informative rather than predictive.

title: Publish the calibration bins even when a bin is too small to read
problem: Hiding thin bins makes calibration look better than it is.
what_changes: A bin table with n and an explicit unreadable marker.
risk: Invites the reader to over-read a bucket of four games.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: bins with enough games track the diagonal. Refutes: a persistent gap that needs a model change.

title: Log every trial, and publish the trial count beside every score
problem: Multiplicity: enough trials produce a good-looking result by chance.
what_changes: An append-only trial log, and a leaderboard column stating the count and the corrected threshold.
risk: Retrospective logging cannot be complete.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: corrected thresholds still admit something. Refutes: nothing survives correction, which is the honest state today.

title: Pre-register the demotion rule now, while nothing is live
problem: A demotion rule written after a strategy fails will be written to excuse it.
what_changes: The same cluster-bootstrap logic, applied in reverse, with a stated sample.
risk: Can retire a strategy that is merely unlucky.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: one live strategy is retired and the retirement is defensible. Refutes: the rule fires constantly on noise, which needs a larger sample.

title: Keep the two model outputs side by side until one wins
problem: Collapsing to one estimator early hides which is better.
what_changes: A gap column between the two outputs, kept until a walk-forward comparison settles it.
risk: Two numbers confuse a casual reader.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: one output wins consistently out of sample. Refutes: they are indistinguishable and the simpler one should be kept.

title: Answer the price question before publishing any backtest
problem: A backtest without prices cannot produce ROI, and calling it a backtest implies it can.
what_changes: A published decision record: what price policy was chosen and why, dated before the first backtest is published.
risk: The answer may be 'no price source at this budget', which caps the project.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: a licence appears. Refutes: no licence is obtainable, in which case the project is a rating project and should say so on the front page.

title: Publish a stale-source banner with the capture age
problem: A page that looks fresh but is nine days old is worse than one that admits it.
what_changes: Per-page capture age and a warning when it exceeds a stated threshold.
risk: A banner on every page becomes noise.
what_would_change_our_mind: Supports: the banner catches a stale page in review. Refutes: the pages are always fresh and the banner is redundant.
